explanation: 802.11ac is Wi-Fi 5 and operates only in the 5 GHz band, which is why it reaches higher rates than 802.11n but has shorter range and fewer legacy clients. 2.4 GHz support in a Wi-Fi 5 access point comes from a separate 802.11n radio.

choices.text: 5 GHz only, marketed as Wi-Fi 5
2.4 GHz only, marketed as Wi-Fi 5
Both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz, marketed as Wi-Fi 4
6 GHz only, marketed as Wi-Fi 6E

stem: Which amendment is marketed as Wi-Fi 7 and introduces multi-link operation?
explanation: 802.11be is Wi-Fi 7. Multi-link operation lets a client use more than one band with the same access point at the same time, and 320 MHz channels widen the pipe further. It builds on the 6 GHz support that Wi-Fi 6E already added.

stem: Which IPv6 prefix contains the global unicast addresses that are routable on the internet?
explanation: 2000::/3 covers the global unicast space that IANA allocates to the registries, which in turn assign blocks to providers and enterprises. FE80::/10 is link-local and never routed, FC00::/7 is unique local, and FF00::/8 is multicast.

stem: Which IPv6 multicast address does a host join so that neighbour solicitation for its address reaches it?
explanation: The solicited-node multicast address is FF02::1:FF00:0/104 with the low 24 bits of the target address appended. A node joins it for every address it configures, so neighbour solicitation is delivered only to hosts whose addresses could match instead of to the whole link.

choices.text: The solicited-node multicast address built from the low 24 bits of the target address
FF02::1, the all-nodes multicast address
FF02::2, the all-routers multicast address
The all-nodes address of the link-local prefix

stem: During duplicate address detection, which source address does a host use while it verifies that its tentative address is unique?
explanation: The host has not yet been allowed to use the tentative address, so it sends the neighbour solicitation from the unspecified address ::. If no neighbour advertisement comes back, it can assign the address. Using the tentative address as the source would defeat the purpose of the check.

choices.text: The unspecified address, ::
The loopback address, ::1
The tentative address being tested
The link-local address of the default gateway

stem: In a spine-leaf fabric, which switch connects the fabric to the WAN, firewalls, and load balancers?
explanation: Spines exist only to move traffic between leaves, so all off-fabric connectivity is placed on border leafs. That keeps the spine tier uniform and puts routing policy, security zones, and external peering at a defined edge point.

choices.text: A border leaf
A spine switch
A core switch in the campus block
An out-of-band management switch

stem: A leaf has 48 ports at 25 Gbps toward servers and four 100 Gbps uplinks to the spines. What does the resulting oversubscription ratio describe?
explanation: Oversubscription compares the bandwidth offered by the downstream ports with the bandwidth available upstream. Here 48 x 25 Gbps is 1.2 Tbps against 400 Gbps of uplink, a 3:1 ratio, which assumes servers will not all demand line rate at once. A lower ratio costs more but reduces contention.

choices.text: The ratio of downstream server bandwidth to upstream uplink bandwidth, here 3:1
The number of spines a single leaf can join at once
The number of MAC addresses the leaf can hold in its table
The ratio of control-plane traffic to data-plane traffic on the spine

stem: How is each link between a leaf and a spine addressed in a routed spine-leaf fabric?
explanation: Every leaf-to-spine link is its own point-to-point subnet, commonly a /31, so each link is a separate Layer 3 hop with no shared broadcast domain. That is what allows equal-cost multipathing over all spines and removes spanning tree from the fabric.

choices.text: As a dedicated point-to-point IP subnet, often a /31, with the leaf and spine as its two endpoints
As part of one large VLAN shared by every leaf and spine
With no IP address at all, since the link only switches frames
From a single management subnet assigned to all fabric ports

stem: An interface must support at least 1,000 hosts. Which prefix length gives the smallest subnet that still satisfies the requirement?
explanation: Work backwards from the host count: 2^10 - 2 = 1,022 usable addresses, which is the first power of two at or above 1,000. Ten host bits means a /22. A /21 would waste 1,022 addresses, and a /23 with only 510 usable hosts falls short.

stem: Which address is a valid host address inside the subnet 192.168.44.0/26?
explanation: A /26 has a block size of 64, so 192.168.44.0/26 spans .0 through .63. The .0 address names the subnet and .63 is its broadcast, leaving .1 through .62 for hosts. The address .64 belongs to the next subnet and is itself a network address.

stem: In a server farm behind a load balancer, clients are configured with one address that the balancer owns rather than a server address. What is that address called?
explanation: Clients send to the virtual IP and the balancer rewrites the destination, or the source in some modes, to a chosen pool member. That indirection is what lets servers be added, drained, or replaced without reconfiguring a single client.

choices.text: A virtual IP address (VIP)
A loopback address configured on every pool member
A DHCP relay address for the server subnet
A floating static route shared by the servers

stem: Why is the spanning-tree root bridge normally placed on a core or distribution switch instead of an access switch?
explanation: Root placement decides which links get blocked. Put the root in the middle of the topology and the blocked ports land where redundancy is cheapest, between access switches, instead of cutting a core uplink that every VLAN depends on. A root stranded at the edge stretches the tree across the whole campus.

choices.text: Because the root sits at the topological centre, so blocked links fall on redundant access paths rather than core links
Because only core and distribution switches run spanning tree
Because access switches cannot be configured as root bridges
Because root placement determines which VLANs an access switch is allowed to carry

stem: What distinguishes multimode fiber from single-mode fiber in a campus backbone?
explanation: Multimode has a wide core that lets several propagation modes travel at once, which suits building and campus runs of a few hundred metres with cheaper optics. Single-mode has a tiny core that carries one mode, holding signal integrity over kilometres but needing costlier laser transceivers.

choices.text: Multimode carries several light paths over shorter, cheaper links; single-mode carries one path over long distances
Multimode uses laser transceivers while single-mode uses LEDs
Multimode is immune to electromagnetic interference while single-mode is not
Multimode caps out at 100 Mb/s while single-mode supports 10 Gb/s

stem: A TCP sender receives three duplicate ACKs for the same sequence number. What does fast retransmit do?
explanation: Duplicate ACKs tell the sender that everything after the gap arrived. Three of them is strong enough evidence of loss that the sender resends the missing segment immediately, then halves the window and continues in fast recovery rather than waiting for a retransmission timer or restarting from slow start.

choices.text: Retransmits the missing segment at once without waiting for the retransmission timer
Halves the congestion window and restarts from slow start
Tears down the connection and reopens it
Retransmits every unacknowledged segment in the window

stem: An IPv6 router decrements a packet's Hop Limit to zero. What does the router do with that packet?
explanation: Hop Limit is the IPv6 equivalent of TTL: hitting zero means the packet has looped or the path is longer than allowed, so the router drops it and reports ICMPv6 Time Exceeded to the source. Traceroute builds on exactly that response.

choices.text: Discards it and returns ICMPv6 Time Exceeded to the source
Forwards it with the Hop Limit reset to 1
Fragments it and rewrites the Hop Limit
Holds it in a queue until a shorter path becomes available

stem: A frame crosses a router on its way to a remote network. Which part of the original PDU does the router discard and rebuild before forwarding?
explanation: A router strips the incoming Layer 2 header and trailer, then builds a new frame header for the outgoing link. The IP packet itself is forwarded unchanged apart from the TTL decrement and header checksum.

choices.text: The data-link frame header and trailer
The IP header
The transport-layer header
The application payload

stem: What is the broadcast address of the subnet that contains the host address 172.20.131.200/21?
explanation: A /21 mask leaves five host bits in the third octet, so subnets step in blocks of eight. 131 falls inside 128-135, which makes 172.20.135.255 the directed broadcast.

stem: A host is configured with the IPv6 address 2001:db8:1:2::a1b2:c3d4. Which solicited-node multicast address does the host join for that address?
explanation: The solicited-node address is ff02::1:ff followed by the low-order 24 bits of the unicast address. The last 32 bits are a1b2c3d4, so the final 24 bits are b2:c3d4.

choices.text: ff02::1:ffb2:c3d4
ff02::1:ffa1:b2c3

stem: A Windows workstation reports the IPv4 address 169.254.37.14 with a mask of 255.255.0.0. What does that address tell a troubleshooter?
explanation: 169.254.0.0/16 is the link-local range a Windows host self-assigns when it cannot reach a DHCP server. The address works only on the local segment and signals a DHCP reachability problem.

choices.text: The host could not reach a DHCP server and self-assigned a link-local address
The host received a valid lease from a DHCP scope in the 169.254.0.0/16 range
The host is using a manually configured RFC 1918 private address
The host has been assigned a loopback alias by the operating system

stem: Why is Category 6A specified instead of Category 6 for a 10GBASE-T run that must reach the full 100-meter channel?
explanation: Category 6A is characterised to 500 MHz and adds alien-crosstalk control that Category 6 lacks, which is what allows 10GBASE-T to reach 100 meters rather than the roughly 55 meters Category 6 supports.

choices.text: Cat 6A is characterised to 500 MHz and controls alien crosstalk, so it carries 10GBASE-T for 100 m
Cat 6A uses a different pinout that doubles the usable pairs
Cat 6A is shielded, which lets it exceed the 100-meter channel limit
Cat 6A is the only category rated for 40GBASE-T at 100 m

stem: In a cloud VPC, how does a security group differ from a network ACL?
explanation: A security group is stateful and attaches to an instance network interface with allow-only rules. A network ACL is stateless, applies at the subnet boundary, and supports both allow and deny statements.

A security group is stateless and applied to a subnet, while a NACL is stateful and attached to an instance

Both are stateless, but only a security group can contain allow rules

stem: Which statement best explains why a container starts in under a second while a virtual machine needs far longer?
explanation: A container shares the host kernel and carries only the application plus its user-space libraries, so there is no guest operating system to boot. A virtual machine boots a full OS image.

choices.text: A container shares the host kernel and packages only the application and its user-space dependencies

A container keeps its filesystem in RAM instead of on disk
A container uses hardware passthrough to skip the boot process

stem: Why does 802.11 use carrier sense multiple access with collision avoidance rather than the collision detection used on wired Ethernet?
explanation: A radio cannot listen for a collision on the same channel while it is transmitting, so collisions can only be avoided rather than detected. 802.11 relies on random backoff, optional RTS/CTS, and positive acknowledgements.

choices.text: A wireless station cannot reliably transmit and listen for collisions on the same channel at once
Wireless frames are too small for collision detection circuitry to resolve
802.11 has no acknowledgements, so collisions must be prevented entirely
The access point assigns every station a dedicated time slot with no contention

stem: A provider sells an MPLS Layer 3 VPN to two customers that both use 10.0.0.0/8 internally. How does the provider keep the overlapping prefixes separate?
explanation: Each customer is bound to its own VRF with a private routing table, and route targets control which prefixes are imported into each VRF. Overlapping addresses therefore never share a forwarding table.

choices.text: Each customer is bound to a separate VRF and route targets control which prefixes are imported
The provider translates both customers into a shared public addressing range
Each customer receives a unique autonomous system number that overrides the overlap
The provider relies on longest-prefix match to distinguish two identical 10.0.0.0/8 advertisements

stem: A stateful firewall drops the return packets of a connection it permitted outbound. Forward and return paths are known to traverse different firewalls. What explains the drop?
explanation: A stateful firewall only permits return traffic that matches an existing session in its own state table. If the reply arrives at a different firewall that never saw the outbound flow, no session exists and the packet is dropped.

choices.text: The returning packets reach a firewall that never observed the outbound flow, so no session exists to match
The firewall ACL is applied in the wrong direction on the inside interface
The connection uses UDP, which stateful inspection cannot track
The firewall NAT pool has been exhausted by earlier sessions

stem: A monitoring host that opens thousands of short-lived HTTP connections to a controller eventually fails new connections with 'Cannot assign requested address'. Which resource is exhausted?
explanation: Each outbound connection consumes an ephemeral source port. Sockets lingering in TIME_WAIT hold their four-tuple, so a high churn of short connections exhausts the local ephemeral port range.

choices.text: The ephemeral source port range, held by sockets in TIME_WAIT
The TCP receive window advertised by the controller
The local ARP cache entry limit
The interface maximum transmission unit

stem: Why do campus designs deliberately limit the size of a single Layer 2 domain?
explanation: Broadcast and unknown-unicast flooding, MAC table size, and the blast radius of a spanning-tree topology change all grow with the Layer 2 domain. Routing between smaller domains contains those effects.

choices.text: Flooding volume and spanning-tree convergence scope grow with the size of the domain

A large Layer 2 domain prevents the use of 802.1Q trunks between switches
MAC addresses must be unique inside a Layer 2 domain and cannot be reused elsewhere

stem: Two switches are joined by a duplex fiber patch cord, but neither interface comes up. Both transceivers are compatible and powered. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: Fiber is directional: each strand carries traffic one way. If transmit is cabled to transmit on both ends, neither receiver ever sees light and the link stays down.

choices.text: The transmit strand at one end is connected to the transmit strand at the other end
The fiber cable is too short for the transceiver to lock onto the signal
The two interfaces are configured with different duplex settings
The SFP modules must both come from the same vendor

stem: An IPv4 header carries an IHL field with the value 15. How long is that header?
explanation: The IHL field counts 32-bit words, not bytes. A value of 15 therefore means 15 times 4, or 60 bytes, which is the maximum an IPv4 header can be once options are included.

choices.text: 60 bytes

40 bytes
64 bytes

stem: What does the Total Length field of an IPv4 header measure?
explanation: Total Length covers the header and the payload together, so a full 1500-byte Ethernet payload reports 1500. Subtracting the IHL-derived header size leaves the actual data length.

choices.text: The header plus the payload, in bytes
Only the payload, in bytes
Only the header, in 32-bit words
The number of routers the packet may still cross

stem: Which IPv4 header field lets a destination group fragments that belong to the same original packet?
explanation: Every fragment of one datagram carries the same Identification value, and the fragment offset then positions it. Together the two fields allow correct reassembly even when fragments arrive out of order.

choices.text: Identification
Total Length
Header Checksum
Protocol

stem: How is the upper-layer protocol identified in an IPv6 packet that carries extension headers?
explanation: Each extension header ends with its own Next Header field, so the value chains forward header by header. The final Next Header value in the chain names the transport protocol or ICMPv6.

A fixed field in the base header always names it, whatever extensions follow

The Payload Length encodes the protocol number

stem: Why does a routed spine-leaf fabric not need spanning tree across the data center?
explanation: Each leaf-to-spine link is its own point-to-point IP subnet, so there is no Layer 2 loop to block. Every uplink can carry traffic at once, and equal-cost multipath spreads flows across them.

choices.text: Every leaf-to-spine link is a routed point-to-point subnet, so no Layer 2 loop exists

Leaves connect to only one spine at a time, which removes any loop
Servers handle loop prevention in software before sending frames

stem: Why is eBGP commonly chosen as the routing protocol between leaves and spines in a large fabric?
explanation: A per-link eBGP session with a unique ASN per switch gives loop-free paths without flooding link state across the whole fabric, and it scales to thousands of nodes while supporting multipath.

choices.text: Unique ASNs per switch give loop-free paths with no fabric-wide link-state flooding and easy multipath

stem: Why does a spine-leaf fabric use spine ports only for fabric uplinks and never for servers?
explanation: Leaving servers off the spines keeps each spine a pure transit tier whose full port count adds bisectional bandwidth. Capacity grows by adding spines, and leaves absorb all server attachment.

choices.text: Keeping spines as pure transit lets every spine port add fabric bandwidth, and growth comes from adding spines

stem: What does a mobility group provide in a multi-controller wireless deployment?
explanation: Controllers in the same mobility group share client context over mobility tunnels, so a client that roams to an AP on another controller keeps its session and does not re-authenticate.

choices.text: It shares client context between controllers so roaming clients keep their sessions
It load-balances CAPWAP control traffic across the wireless management VLAN
It synchronises the WLC configuration database between controllers
It assigns radio channels and transmit power to access points

stem: What does an access point do when it is placed in monitor mode?
explanation: A monitor-mode AP stops serving clients and dedicates its radio to passively capturing frames for intrusion detection and site surveys. It is a sensor, not an access point for users.

choices.text: It stops serving clients and passively captures wireless traffic for analysis
It serves clients but forwards their traffic locally instead of to the controller
It becomes a backup controller for the APs in its mobility group
It converts its radio to a dedicated backhaul link between buildings

stem: Ping replies to a remote site are fast, but large file transfers to that site crawl. No interface shows errors and the link is not saturated. What best explains the throughput?
explanation: A TCP sender may have only one window in flight per round trip, so throughput is capped near window size divided by RTT. Long paths therefore need a larger window to fill the link, even when latency looks fine to a ping.

choices.text: Throughput is limited by the TCP window divided by the round-trip time
The path MTU is smaller than the server's interface MTU, so every frame is dropped
The remote site's DNS server is answering slowly
The client NIC is negotiating half duplex with the access switch

stem: Users report strong Wi-Fi signal but slow throughput, and the problem worsens as more people join the same area. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: Signal strength says nothing about airtime. When many clients share one channel they contend for the same medium, so each station waits longer and aggregate throughput per client falls.

choices.text: Clients on the same channel are contending for airtime
The AP transmit power is too low for the coverage area
The clients are receiving addresses from the wrong DHCP scope
The SSID is hidden, so clients must probe more often

stem: Which combination of amendment and spectrum defines Wi-Fi 6E?
explanation: Wi-Fi 6E is 802.11ax operating in the newly opened 6 GHz band. The PHY is the same as Wi-Fi 6; the E denotes the additional spectrum, which supplies many more non-overlapping channels.

choices.text: 802.11ax extended into the 6 GHz band
802.11ac extended into the 6 GHz band
802.11be restricted to the 5 GHz band
802.11n extended into the 60 GHz band

stem: Which modulation scheme did 802.11ac introduce that 802.11n does not use?
explanation: 802.11ac added 256-QAM, carrying eight bits per subcarrier instead of the six of 64-QAM. The denser constellation demands a better signal-to-noise ratio to stay decodable.

choices.text: 256-QAM
64-QAM
DSSS with Barker coding
Binary phase-shift keying

stem: What is the widest channel 802.11n can use?
explanation: 802.11n introduced channel bonding but caps it at two 20 MHz channels, giving 40 MHz. Wider 80 and 160 MHz channels only arrived with 802.11ac.

choices.text: 40 MHz
20 MHz
80 MHz
160 MHz

stem: What is the maximum channel length for a twisted-pair Ethernet link such as 100BASE-TX or 1000BASE-T?
explanation: The 100-meter channel budget covers up to 90 m of permanently installed horizontal cable plus 10 m of patch cords at each end. Exceeding it causes attenuation and crosstalk failures that show up as CRC errors.

choices.text: 100 meters
90 meters
500 meters
185 meters

stem: Which fiber medium is required to carry 10GBASE-ER across its full 40-kilometer reach?
explanation: 10GBASE-ER uses 1550 nm optics over single-mode fiber to reach 40 km. Multimode grades lose too much signal over that distance, so OM1 or OM3 would fall far short.

choices.text: Single-mode fiber
OM1 multimode fiber
OM3 multimode fiber
Category 6A twisted pair

stem: How many equal /27 subnets can be carved out of the address block 10.0.0.0/24?
explanation: A /27 borrows three host bits from a /24, and two to the third power is eight. Each resulting subnet holds 32 addresses, 30 of which are usable.

stem: Which prefix length provides exactly 62 usable host addresses on a subnet?
explanation: A /26 leaves six host bits, so the block contains 64 addresses. Subtracting the network and broadcast addresses leaves 62 usable hosts.

stem: In a conventional /64 IPv6 subnet, how many bits make up the interface identifier?
explanation: A /64 splits the 128-bit address in half: the first 64 bits are the subnet prefix and the remaining 64 bits identify the interface. That width is what makes stateless address autoconfiguration practical.

stem: Which IPv6 prefix is reserved for use in documentation and examples?
explanation: RFC 3849 sets aside 2001:db8::/32 for documentation so examples never collide with real global unicast space. Lab topologies and textbooks use it for exactly that reason.

stem: At which OSI layer does a repeater or hub operate?
explanation: A repeater regenerates the electrical signal without reading addresses or headers, so it works purely at the physical layer. That is why a hub extends a collision domain rather than dividing it.

choices.text: Physical
Data link
Network
Transport

stem: Which two OSI layers correspond to the network access layer of the TCP/IP model?
explanation: The TCP/IP network access layer covers everything below IP, so it absorbs the OSI data-link and physical layers. The internet layer maps to OSI network, and the transport layer stays one-to-one.

choices.text: Data link and physical
Network and transport
Session and presentation
Transport and application

stem: What is the role of a CSU/DSU on a legacy serial WAN circuit?
explanation: The channel service unit terminates the provider's digital line and the data service unit converts between line signalling and the router's serial interface. Modern handoffs usually fold both functions into the provider demarcation device.

choices.text: It terminates the digital carrier circuit and presents a serial interface to the router
It converts copper Ethernet to fiber
It load-balances traffic across two circuits
It encrypts traffic before it enters the provider network

stem: What does a service level agreement on a business WAN circuit typically guarantee?
explanation: An SLA is a contractual performance envelope covering uptime, one-way delay, delay variation, and time to repair. Pricing and CPE management are separate commercial terms.

choices.text: Availability, latency, jitter, and repair time targets
A fixed monthly price for all bandwidth upgrades
That the provider will manage the customer's routers
Unlimited bandwidth with no committed rate

stem: What does a virtual machine snapshot capture?
explanation: A snapshot records the current disk, and optionally memory, so the VM can be reverted to that instant. It is not a backup, because it normally lives on the same storage as the running VM.

choices.text: The VM's disk and memory state at a point in time for rollback
A full backup copy stored on a remote tape library
A container image exported for reuse on another host
A copy of the hypervisor's global configuration only

stem: Why do multiple containers built from the same image use less disk space than the equivalent number of virtual machines?
explanation: Container images are stacked read-only layers that many containers can share, with a thin writable layer on top. Virtual machines each carry a complete guest operating system image.

choices.text: Their read-only image layers are shared and only the writable layer is unique
Containers compress their filesystems automatically at runtime
Containers store their data in RAM instead of on disk
Each container mounts the host filesystem read-only

stem: What does a reverse proxy placed in front of web servers provide?
explanation: A reverse proxy is the public face of a service: clients connect to it and it relays requests to one or more backends. That hides server topology and centralizes TLS, caching, and request filtering.

choices.text: It accepts client requests and forwards them to backend servers, hiding the servers and often terminating TLS
It caches DNS answers for internal clients
It assigns addresses to guests on the wireless LAN
It inspects outbound traffic from internal users

stem: What does a network access control deployment check before admitting a device to the network?
explanation: NAC combines authentication with a posture check, so a known device running outdated antivirus or missing patches can be quarantined. Admission depends on both who the device is and what state it is in.

choices.text: The device's identity and its compliance with policy such as patch level or endpoint protection
The device's routing table for a usable default route
The speed of the switch port the device is plugged into
Whether the device already holds a DHCP reservation

stem: Instances in a cloud VPC have no public IP addresses but must reach internet destinations. Which component performs the outbound address translation?
explanation: A NAT gateway sits in a public subnet and translates the private source addresses of instances in private subnets as their traffic leaves the VPC. Return traffic is mapped back to the originating instance, so no inbound path is created.

choices.text: A NAT gateway in a public subnet
An internet gateway alone
A route table local entry
A security group outbound rule

stem: In a site-to-site VPN between an on-premises network and a cloud provider, which device is represented by the customer gateway object?
explanation: The customer gateway is the cloud-side reference to the customer's own VPN endpoint, normally the on-premises router or firewall that terminates the tunnel. The virtual private gateway is the provider-side endpoint.

choices.text: The on-premises router or firewall terminating the tunnel
The provider-side VPN concentrator
The cloud NAT instance
The provider's internet gateway

stem: An access point is mounted where no power outlet exists. Which connection supplies both data and electrical power to the AP?
explanation: The AP's Ethernet uplink connects to a switch port that delivers Power over Ethernet, so a single cable carries the CAPWAP or management traffic and the DC power the AP needs. A local power injector achieves the same result when the switch cannot supply PoE.

choices.text: The Ethernet uplink to a PoE-capable switch port
The console port
A USB service port
The 5 GHz radio interface

stem: Where is an edge firewall normally placed in a campus topology?
explanation: The edge firewall sits between the ISP handoff and the internal network so every packet entering or leaving the site is inspected and filtered. Placing it inside the core would leave the WAN link itself unprotected.

choices.text: Between the ISP handoff and the internal network
Between the access and distribution layers
On each access switch uplink
Inside the data center between servers

stem: Widening a 5 GHz channel from 20 MHz to 40 MHz raises the theoretical throughput. What is the main cost of that change?
explanation: Bonding two 20 MHz channels consumes twice the spectrum, which halves the number of non-overlapping channels available in the band. In a dense deployment the wider channels overlap more often, so co-channel interference and retries increase.

choices.text: Fewer non-overlapping channels, so more co-channel interference
Lower client transmit power
Loss of WPA2 support
Inability to use 802.11ac

stem: How does an 802.11 station confirm that a unicast data frame arrived intact?
explanation: The receiving station waits a short interframe space and returns an acknowledgement frame. If the sender does not receive that ACK it assumes loss and retransmits, which is why wireless throughput falls quickly as retries climb.

choices.text: The receiver returns an ACK frame after a short interframe space
The sender waits for a TCP acknowledgement from the client
The access point broadcasts a delivery report
The frame's FCS is echoed back in the next beacon

stem: A host sends a packet to a destination on a different subnet. Whose MAC address does it place in the frame?
explanation: The host compares the destination against its own mask, sees that the target is off-subnet, and forwards the frame to its default gateway. The destination IP stays the remote host, but the frame carries the gateway MAC so the local segment can deliver it.

choices.text: The default gateway MAC address
The remote destination MAC address
The broadcast MAC address
Its own MAC address

stem: Which dotted-decimal subnet mask corresponds to a /21 prefix?
explanation: A /21 keeps 21 network bits, so the mask has 21 ones followed by 11 zeros: 255.255.248.0. The third octet contributes 11111000 in binary, which is 248.

stem: What is the principal trade-off of a collapsed-core campus design?
explanation: Collapsing distribution and core into one layer cuts cost, cabling, and hop count, but the same devices now carry all inter-VLAN and WAN traffic. Failure of a collapsed-core switch removes redundancy for a large portion of the campus and limits how far the design can scale.

choices.text: Lower cost and fewer hops, but reduced redundancy and scaling headroom
Higher cost but simpler troubleshooting
Better wireless roaming but no wired VLAN support
Guaranteed loop-free topology without STP

stem: A laptop is moved from VLAN 10 to VLAN 20 but keeps its old VLAN 10 address. Why does it not simply obtain a new address immediately?
explanation: A DHCP client keeps its lease and first tries to renew at the 50 percent timer by unicasting to the original server. That server is no longer reachable in the new broadcast domain, so the client must wait for renewal to fail or be told to release before it broadcasts a fresh discovery.

choices.text: It renews at the 50 percent timer and the old server is unreachable in the new VLAN
The switch rewrites the source MAC so DHCP cannot match the request
ARP caching prevents any broadcast from being sent
The default gateway blocks all UDP traffic

stem: A router shows an ARP entry in the incomplete state for a next hop. What does that state tell you?
explanation: Incomplete means the router sent ARP requests but received no reply, so it has no MAC address to build the frame with. Packets destined through that next hop are dropped until resolution succeeds.

choices.text: No ARP reply was received, so frames to that next hop cannot be built
The entry is cached but expired and will refresh from the routing table
The next hop resolved to a multicast MAC address
The interface is administratively down

stem: What reach does Category 6A twisted-pair cabling support for 10GBASE-T?
explanation: Cat 6A is specified for 10GBASE-T over a 100-meter channel because its improved shielding and reduced alien crosstalk keep the signal usable at 500 MHz. Cat 6 is limited to about 55 meters for the same speed.

choices.text: 100 meters
55 meters
220 meters
500 meters

stem: Why are the pairs inside unshielded twisted-pair cable twisted around each other?
explanation: The twist rate differs per pair so that externally induced noise and crosstalk from neighbouring pairs couple equally into both conductors. Because the interference appears as a common-mode signal, it cancels at the receiver instead of corrupting the differential data signal.

choices.text: So induced noise couples equally into both wires and cancels at the receiver
To increase the cable's tensile strength
To allow the pairs to carry DC power
To reduce the cable's capacitance to the building ground

stem: How does TCP slow start increase the amount of data a sender may have in flight?
explanation: The sender begins with a small congestion window and grows it by roughly one segment per acknowledgement, effectively doubling the window each round-trip time. Growth continues until the window reaches the slow-start threshold or a loss is detected.

choices.text: The congestion window doubles each round-trip until the slow-start threshold
The receive window is fixed and the sender fills it immediately
The sender retransmits every segment twice to measure loss
The window grows by one segment per second regardless of acknowledgements

stem: A TCP receiver gets segments 5, 6, 8, and 9 after already receiving segment 4. What does it send back, and why?
explanation: The receiver buffers the out-of-order segments and keeps returning duplicate acknowledgements for the last in-order byte, which is segment 4's sequence space. After three duplicate ACKs the sender treats the gap as lost and retransmits segment 7 without waiting for a timer.

choices.text: Duplicate ACKs for the missing segment, which trigger a fast retransmit
A reset, because out-of-order delivery is always fatal
ACKs for segments 8 and 9, discarding segment 7
Nothing until the retransmission timer expires

stem: In a split-MAC wireless architecture, how do the CAPWAP control and data paths differ by default?
explanation: The control tunnel runs over UDP 5246 and is DTLS-encrypted to protect management exchanges between AP and controller. The data tunnel uses UDP 5247 and is not encrypted by default, because the client payload is usually already protected by 802.11 encryption.

choices.text: Control uses UDP 5246 and is DTLS-encrypted; data uses UDP 5247 and is unencrypted by default
Both tunnels share UDP 5246 and are encrypted by default
Control uses TCP 5246 and data uses TCP 5247
Data uses UDP 5246 and control uses UDP 5247, both in clear text

stem: Which OSI layer is the only one that appends both a header and a trailer to the data it receives from the layer above?
explanation: The data-link layer wraps the network-layer packet in a frame header and adds a trailer holding the frame check sequence. No other layer attaches a trailer, which makes the frame the only PDU with fields at both ends.

choices.text: Data link
Network
Transport
Session

stem: Which OSI layer defines the voltage levels, connector types, and pin assignments used on a cable?
explanation: The physical layer is the only layer concerned with the mechanical and electrical specification of the medium. Voltages, pinouts, and connector shapes are all physical-layer details; framing and addressing sit above it.

choices.text: Physical
Data link
Network
Transport

stem: An IPv6 packet carries a Next Header value of 58. Which protocol does the payload contain?
explanation: Value 58 identifies ICMPv6. ICMPv6 carries neighbour discovery, router advertisements, and echo messages, and it is the protocol most IPv6 control-plane functions depend on. TCP is 6 and UDP is 17.

choices.text: ICMPv6
TCP
UDP
OSPFv3

stem: How many bits long is the Flow Label field in the IPv6 base header?
explanation: The Flow Label is 20 bits, sitting between the 8-bit Traffic Class and the 16-bit Payload Length. Its combined field of Traffic Class plus Flow Label occupies 28 bits, leaving the version nibble to complete the first 32-bit word.

choices.text: 20 bits
8 bits
16 bits
32 bits

stem: Which statement describes the difference between SC and LC fiber connectors?
explanation: SC uses a square push-pull body with a 2.5 mm ferrule, while LC is roughly half the size, uses a 1.25 mm ferrule, and latches like an RJ-style clip. LC therefore allows roughly double the port density on a patch panel.

choices.text: LC is smaller and latches, SC is larger and pushes straight in
SC is smaller and latches, LC is larger and pushes straight in
Both use a 1.25 mm ferrule and differ only in colour
SC is used only for single-mode and LC only for multimode

stem: What does a cable category rating such as Cat 6 actually specify?
explanation: A category rating specifies the maximum frequency the cable must support and the associated insertion loss, crosstalk, and return-loss limits. It does not mandate a particular Ethernet speed; a standard such as 1000BASE-T is what maps a speed onto a category.

choices.text: The maximum frequency and performance limits the cable must meet
The maximum cable length that the standard permits
The exact Ethernet speed the cable will always run at
The shielding material used around each conductor pair

stem: How does an out-of-band management network reach a switch that has lost all data-plane connectivity?
explanation: Out-of-band management connects each device console or aux port to a terminal server, giving a path that does not depend on the production network. Because it uses a separate physical and logical path, it still works when the data plane, routing, or the device IP stack is broken.

choices.text: Through the console or aux port wired to a terminal server
Through an SSH session to the management SVI
Through the loopback address reachable over the routed core
Through an SNMP trap sent to the NMS server

stem: In a routed-access campus design, where does the Layer 2 domain end?
explanation: In routed access the access switch itself is the Layer 3 gateway, so the Layer 2 boundary is the access switch uplink. Every uplink to the distribution or core layer is a routed point-to-point link, which removes spanning tree from the campus and shrinks each failure domain to a single closet.

choices.text: At the access switch uplink, which is a routed point-to-point link
At the distribution switch trunk toward the core
At the core switch where VLANs are terminated
At the WAN edge router interface

stem: A single link between one leaf and one spine fails in a spine-leaf fabric running ECMP. What is the result?
explanation: Equal-cost multipathing simply removes the failed path from the hash and spreads flows across the remaining spines. There is no blocked port and no spanning-tree reconvergence, so traffic keeps flowing with only the fabric bisection bandwidth reduced.

choices.text: Traffic is rehashed over the remaining equal-cost paths with no STP event
Spanning tree blocks the leaf uplink and reconverges over 30 seconds
The leaf loses all connectivity until the link is restored
The fabric elects a new root bridge for that leaf

stem: Why is VXLAN typically used on top of a spine-leaf fabric?
explanation: VXLAN builds a Layer 2 overlay across a Layer 3 underlay, so segments can span racks and workloads can move without re-addressing. The underlay stays a simple routed fabric where every spine-to-leaf link is forwarding, and the overlay carries the large tenant address space.

choices.text: It provides a Layer 2 overlay over the Layer 3 underlay for large segments
It replaces the need for a routing protocol in the underlay
It removes the need for MAC address learning on the leaf switches
It compresses tenant traffic so fewer uplinks are needed

stem: A container is deleted and recreated from the same image. Which mechanism keeps its data across that cycle?
explanation: A persistent volume is storage provisioned outside the container filesystem and mounted into it. Because the volume lifecycle is independent of the container, recreating the container reattaches the same data, whereas the writable layer of the old container is discarded.

choices.text: A persistent volume mounted into the container
The writable layer inside the old container
The container image itself
The container runtime cache

stem: A hypervisor is configured to run virtual machines whose combined RAM allocation exceeds the physical memory installed. What makes this possible?
explanation: Memory overcommit relies on the hypervisor reclaiming pages that guests have not touched, using ballooning, transparent page sharing, and swapping to a datastore. It works because guests rarely use every allocated byte at the same moment; if they do, performance collapses or the host runs out of memory.

choices.text: The hypervisor reclaims idle guest pages through ballooning and swapping
Each guest is given a private copy of physical RAM on demand
The CPU throttles guests so their memory needs shrink
The guest operating systems share a single kernel address space

stem: In a service provider WAN, which device is the customer edge?
explanation: The customer edge is the equipment on the customer premises that hands off to the provider, typically a router or firewall owned or managed by the customer. The provider edge is the provider-owned device on the other end of that handoff link.

choices.text: The customer-owned device that hands off to the provider network
The provider device that terminates the customer access circuit
The provider backbone router inside the core
The internet exchange switch shared by many providers

stem: Which MEF service type gives a customer any-to-any connectivity among three or more sites?
explanation: E-LAN is a multipoint-to-multipoint service, so every site can reach every other site through a single logical LAN. E-Line is point-to-point, and E-Tree is rooted multipoint where leaves may only talk to the root.

choices.text: E-LAN, a multipoint-to-multipoint service
E-Line, a point-to-point service
E-Tree, a rooted multipoint service
A dedicated leased line per site pair

stem: An email gateway flags an attachment as suspicious but cannot identify it from signatures. Which control determines whether it is malicious before delivery?
explanation: A sandbox executes the file in an isolated instrumented environment and observes what it attempts to do, such as writing to autorun keys or contacting a command-and-control host. Behavioural detonation catches unknown malware that signature matching cannot classify.

choices.text: Detonating the file in an isolated sandbox and watching its behaviour
Matching the file hash against the antivirus signature database
Blocking the attachment based on its file extension
Quarantining every attachment that contains macros

stem: Why must an inline intrusion prevention system decrypt TLS sessions to inspect them?
explanation: TLS hides the application payload from anything between the endpoints, so an inline sensor sees only ciphertext and record headers. Decryption, typically through a trusted certificate on the sensor, restores the plaintext the signature engine needs; without it the device can only profile metadata.

choices.text: The payload is ciphertext, so signatures cannot match without decryption
The sensor needs the session keys to forward packets upstream
Decryption is required to preserve the packet ordering
TLS resets the connection when a passive device observes it

stem: What distinguishes a public subnet from a private subnet in a cloud VPC?
explanation: A public subnet has a route table entry pointing default traffic at an internet gateway, so resources with public addresses are reachable from the internet. A private subnet has no such route and relies on a NAT device for outbound-only access.

choices.text: Its route table points to an internet gateway
It uses a different private address range
It has a larger CIDR block than a private subnet
Its security groups allow inbound traffic by default

stem: Which cloud addressing feature provides a static public IPv4 address that can be detached from one instance and attached to another?
explanation: An elastic IP is allocated to the account rather than to an instance, so it can be remapped during failover while clients keep using the same destination address. A normal public address is tied to the instance and released when the instance stops.

choices.text: An elastic IP address
A public IPv4 address assigned at launch
A private address in the VPC CIDR
A carrier-grade NAT address from the provider

stem: An engineer must divide 10.20.0.0/16 into exactly 12 equal-sized subnets and keep as many hosts per subnet as possible. Which mask should be used?
explanation: Twelve subnets needs at least 4 subnet bits, because 2^4 gives 16 and 2^3 gives only 8. Borrowing 4 bits from the 16-bit host portion yields /20, which still leaves 12 host bits and 4094 usable addresses. A /19 would produce only 8 subnets and a /21 would waste host space.

choices.text: /21 and /22 combined

stem: A point-to-point link between two routers is addressed with a /31 prefix. How many usable host addresses does that subnet provide under RFC 3021?
explanation: RFC 3021 permits /31 on point-to-point links, where both addresses are usable because no network or broadcast address is reserved. A /30 wastes two of its four addresses for exactly that purpose, which is why /31 is preferred on router-to-router links.

stem: A host has the address 192.168.1.130 with mask 255.255.255.192. Which address is its directed broadcast address?
explanation: A /26 mask splits the last octet into 64-address blocks, so 130 falls inside the 128 to 191 range. The network address is 192.168.1.128 and the broadcast is 192.168.1.191; 192.168.1.255 would be the broadcast only under a /24 mask.

stem: An IPv6 host must resolve a neighbour link-layer address. To which address does it send the Neighbor Solicitation?
explanation: Neighbor Solicitation goes to the target's solicited-node multicast address, formed from ff02::1:ff00:0/104 plus the low 24 bits of the target address. Only the intended host and a small set of others process the message, instead of every node on the link.

choices.text: The target solicited-node multicast address
The target link-local unicast address

stem: A router advertisement carries a prefix length of /72. Why does this break stateless address autoconfiguration on the attached hosts?
explanation: SLAAC builds the interface identifier in the low 64 bits and takes the remaining bits from the advertised prefix, so the prefix must be exactly /64. A /72 leaves only 56 bits for the identifier and hosts reject or misapply the prefix, which is why non-/64 RAs are not supported for SLAAC.

choices.text: SLAAC requires a /64 so the 64-bit interface identifier fits
/72 prefixes are reserved for point-to-point links
Hosts reject any prefix longer than /48
It disables Duplicate Address Detection but not addressing

stem: An IPv6 packet carries both a Hop-by-Hop Options header and a Destination Options header. Which one must appear first?
explanation: RFC 8200 requires Hop-by-Hop Options to be the first extension header so every router along the path can act on it. Destination Options meant only for the final destination come later, after any routing header.

choices.text: Hop-by-Hop Options
Destination Options
Fragment
Either order is acceptable

stem: A TCP receiver advertises a window size of zero. What must the sender do?
explanation: A zero window means the receive buffer is full, so the sender stops transmitting data and periodically sends zero-window probes to learn when space is available. Continuing to retransmit would only add load to a receiver that is already unable to accept data.

choices.text: Retransmit the last segment immediately
Stop sending and send zero-window probes
Tear down the connection
Halve the maximum segment size

stem: A TCP sender using path MTU discovery receives an ICMP fragmentation-needed message. Why does it reduce its maximum segment size?
explanation: The ICMP message reports the smallest MTU on the path, which is below the segment size the sender was using. Because the Don't Fragment bit prevented fragmentation, the packet could not be forwarded at all, so the sender must shrink its segments to fit that link.

choices.text: ICMP errors always halve the congestion window
The reported MTU is smaller than the segment size, so packets could not be forwarded unfragmented
The receiver buffer is full
The retransmission timer expired

stem: Which property makes single-mode fiber suitable for links several kilometres long while multimode fiber is limited to shorter runs?
explanation: Single-mode fiber has a very small core that supports essentially one propagation path, so modal dispersion is negligible and the signal stays readable over long distances. Multimode fiber carries many paths that arrive at slightly different times, which smears the pulse and caps the distance.

choices.text: Single-mode uses cheaper light sources
Single-mode has a small core carrying one propagation mode, so modal dispersion is negligible
Multimode has lower attenuation per kilometre
Single-mode carries several wavelengths at once

stem: 802.11n raised throughput over 802.11g mainly through which pair of techniques?
explanation: 802.11n introduced MIMO spatial streams and optional 40 MHz channels, both of which increase the amount of data sent per unit of airtime. OFDMA and MU-MIMO belong to 802.11ax, while 1024-QAM and 160 MHz channels belong to 802.11ac.

choices.text: OFDMA and MU-MIMO
MIMO spatial streams and 40 MHz channel bonding
1024-QAM and 160 MHz channels
SAE and protected management frames

stem: A unified wireless deployment uses CAPWAP. Which statement describes the split between its two channels?
explanation: CAPWAP control runs over UDP 5246 and the optional data tunnel over UDP 5247. The control channel carries join requests, configuration, and keepalives, while the data channel carries client frames only when the WLAN is centrally switched rather than locally switched.

choices.text: Control on UDP 5246 and data on UDP 5247
Control on TCP 5246 and data on TCP 5247
Both channels share UDP 5247
Control on UDP 5247 and data on UDP 5246

stem: Which device marks the boundary between the service provider responsibility and the enterprise responsibility on a WAN circuit?
explanation: The network interface device, often called the demarc or smart jack, is the demarcation point. Beyond it the provider owns and maintains the circuit; inside it the enterprise owns the cabling and the terminating equipment.

choices.text: The core switch
The network interface device at the demarc
The edge router LAN interface
The firewall outside interface

stem: A Layer 2 switch forwards a frame without inspecting its payload. Which layers of the OSI model are actually involved in that decision?
explanation: The switch receives bits at Layer 1 and reads the frame header at Layer 2 to find the destination hardware address. The network-layer payload is never examined, which is exactly why a VLAN can carry IPv4, IPv6, or any other protocol transparently.

choices.text: Layers 1 and 2
Layers 2 and 3
Layers 1, 2 and 3
Layer 2 only

stem: A workstation on a user VLAN cannot reach any server and reports the address 169.254.14.9/16. Which conclusion is best supported by that address?
explanation: 169.254.0.0/16 is the link-local range a host self-assigns when no DHCP server answers. The interface is up and has an address, so the fault lies in DHCP reachability or in the relay configuration rather than in the physical link.

choices.text: Only the default gateway is down
DHCP did not deliver a lease, so the host self-assigned a link-local address
The host received a valid public address
Routing works but NAT is failing

stem: An IPv4 header contains options, so the header is padded with zeros before the payload begins. What does that padding guarantee?
explanation: The Header Length field counts 32-bit words, so options must be padded to a whole word. Without the padding the IHL value could not describe the header exactly, and the receiver would misplace the start of the payload.

choices.text: That the Total Length field stays a whole number of bytes
That the header checksum covers the options
That the header ends on a 32-bit boundary so the payload starts at a known offset
That routers can fragment the packet on any byte boundary

stem: In an ad hoc wireless network, how do the client stations communicate?
explanation: An ad hoc network is an independent basic service set (IBSS): the stations talk directly to each other with no access point and no distribution system. An infrastructure BSS instead sends every frame through an AP, which is how a home or enterprise WLAN normally works.

choices.text: They send all traffic through a central access point
They communicate directly with each other without an access point or distribution system
They tunnel frames to a wireless LAN controller inside CAPWAP
They forward frames between radios using the switch MAC address table

stem: A fragment arrives with the IPv4 Fragment Offset field set to 185. At what byte offset in the original datagram does this fragment's payload begin?
explanation: Fragment Offset is expressed in 8-byte units, so the byte offset is 185 x 8 = 1,480. Interpretation in bytes directly is the classic mistake; the field is 13 bits wide.

stem: Which value appears in the Version field of an IPv4 header?
explanation: The Version field is 4 bits and holds 4 for IPv4 and 6 for IPv6. 20 is the minimum header length in bytes without options, and 32 is the bit width of an IPv4 address, not a Version value.

stem: Which portion of an IPv4 packet does the header checksum protect?
explanation: The header checksum covers only the header. Every router that decrements TTL must recompute it, so protecting the payload with it would force a full recalculation at each hop; payload integrity is left to the TCP or UDP checksum.

choices.text: The entire packet including the payload
The payload only
The header only
The header and the first 8 bytes of payload

stem: Which interframe space is the shortest, and is used by a station that must send an immediate response such as an ACK?
explanation: SIFS is the shortest interframe space, which gives ACKs, CTS frames, and fragment bursts priority over stations waiting through DIFS for normal contention. DIFS is used for new transmissions, and PIFS and EIFS are longer still.

choices.text: DIFS
PIFS
EIFS
SIFS

stem: Which set of channels is the only non-overlapping group in the 2.4 GHz band in North America?
explanation: 2.4 GHz channels are spaced only 5 MHz apart while a 20 MHz channel needs roughly 20 to 22 MHz, so 1, 6, and 11 are the non-overlapping set. Channels 36, 40, and 44 belong to the 5 GHz band.

stem: How does an autonomous access point differ from a lightweight access point?
explanation: An autonomous AP holds its own configuration, bridges client traffic locally, and is managed one device at a time. A lightweight AP keeps almost no configuration of its own and depends on a wireless LAN controller for its configuration and for the CAPWAP tunnels that carry client traffic.

choices.text: An autonomous AP is configured individually and handles its own switching and management, while a lightweight AP relies on a WLC
An autonomous AP cannot function without a WLC managing its radios
A lightweight AP keeps its full configuration locally and only reports statistics to the WLC
An autonomous AP can only operate in monitor mode

stem: A team rents virtual machines and then installs and patches its own operating system, middleware, and runtime. Which cloud service model is this?
explanation: In IaaS the provider supplies virtualized compute, storage, and networking, while the customer manages everything from the guest OS upward. PaaS would supply the runtime, SaaS would supply the whole application, and FaaS would supply only function execution.

choices.text: SaaS
PaaS
IaaS
FaaS

stem: Which cable type connects a workstation's serial port to a Cisco device's console port?
explanation: A rollover cable reverses the pin order from one end to the other, pairing pin 1 with pin 8, and is used with a terminal emulator for out-of-band console access. Straight-through and crossover cables are for Ethernet, not console access.

choices.text: Straight-through
Crossover
Rollover
Coaxial

stem: What is the receiving host doing when it removes the header, and trailer where present, that the sender added at each layer?
explanation: De-encapsulation is the reverse of encapsulation: each layer strips its own control information and passes the payload up. Encapsulation happens on transmit, while segmentation and multiplexing describe how data is divided and shared, not how headers are removed.

choices.text: Encapsulation
De-encapsulation
Segmentation
Multiplexing

stem: What distinguishes an IPv6 anycast address from a unicast address?
explanation: An anycast address is assigned to several interfaces, and the routing system delivers each packet to whichever member is nearest by routing metric. Multicast is the one-to-many service, and fe80::/10 is the link-local unicast range.

choices.text: It is delivered to every interface that shares the address
It is only valid on point-to-point links
It must be configured from the fe80::/10 range
It is assigned to multiple interfaces and delivered to the nearest one

stem: What is the purpose of the 7-byte preamble and the 1-byte start frame delimiter at the beginning of an Ethernet frame?
explanation: The alternating bits of the preamble let the receiver lock its clock onto the incoming signal, and the final 10101011 pattern of the SFD marks where the frame proper begins. Addresses and EtherType follow in the frame header, and error detection is done by the trailing FCS.

choices.text: They carry the destination MAC address
They let the receiver synchronize its clock to the bit stream and mark the start of the frame
They provide the frame check sequence for the payload
They identify the EtherType of the encapsulated protocol

stem: Which MAC address prefix is used for IPv4 multicast frames on Ethernet?
explanation: IPv4 multicast maps into the 01:00:5e:00:00:00/24 range, with the low 23 bits of the group address copied into the MAC. 33:33 is the IPv6 multicast prefix, and ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff is the broadcast address.

choices.text: ff:ff:ff

stem: What does the SX designation in 1000BASE-SX indicate?
explanation: SX means short wavelength: an 850 nm laser over multimode fiber, typically reaching 220 to 550 m depending on the fiber grade. LX is the 1310 nm long-wavelength variant, T is twisted pair, and CX is twinaxial copper.

choices.text: Single-mode fiber with a 1310 nm laser
Twinaxial copper cable
Category 5e twisted pair
Multimode fiber with an 850 nm short-wavelength laser

stem: How are ARP request and ARP reply frames addressed at layer 2?
explanation: The request must reach every station on the segment because the sender does not yet know the target's MAC, so it is broadcast. The reply goes straight back to the station that asked, so it is unicast even though the requester's address was learned from a broadcast.

choices.text: The request is broadcast and the reply is unicast to the sender
Both are broadcast
The request is unicast and the reply is broadcast
Both are unicast

stem: A switch records the source address 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E. Which portion of that address was assigned by the IEEE to identify the manufacturer?
explanation: The first 24 bits are the Organizationally Unique Identifier, burned in by the IEEE to the vendor; the vendor assigns the remaining 24 bits per interface. That is why one vendor's adapters share the first three bytes and differ in the last three.

choices.text: The first 24 bits, which form the Organizationally Unique Identifier
The last 24 bits, which are reserved for the vendor
The first 8 bits, which encode the device type
All 48 bits, because the whole address is registered to one vendor

stem: An IPv6 address is written as eight groups of four hexadecimal digits. How many bits does that represent?
explanation: Eight groups of 16 bits is 128 bits. That is four times the IPv4 address space width, which is why an IPv6 subnet is normally a /64 and still leaves 64 host bits.

choices.text: 32 bits
64 bits
128 bits
256 bits

stem: In a structured campus cabling design, what is the role of an IDF?
explanation: The intermediate distribution frame is the floor or building wiring closet that terminates horizontal cabling from end devices and uplinks to the main distribution frame. The MDF is the campus cross-connect where the WAN demarc and core meet.

choices.text: It is the floor-level wiring closet that aggregates horizontal cabling and uplinks to the MDF
It is the single cross-connect where the carrier demarcation and core switching meet
It is the redundant core switch pair that forwards inter-VLAN traffic
It is the device that terminates the ISP circuit and performs NAT

stem: Why would a factory run machine-vision inference on a server on the plant floor instead of in a distant public cloud region?
explanation: That is edge computing: processing happens near the data source, so control decisions are not delayed by a WAN round trip and the volume of raw video that must be uploaded drops sharply. Cloud is still used for training and long-term storage.

choices.text: To cut the round-trip latency to the process and avoid uploading every raw frame
Because cloud compute is always more expensive than on-premises hardware
Because inference models cannot be licensed for cloud use
To avoid having to encrypt traffic between the plant and the cloud

stem: Why is an on-site RF survey preferred over a predictive model for a warehouse with tall metal racking?
explanation: Racking blocks and reflects 5 GHz energy in ways a floor-plan model cannot capture, so measured signal, interference, and channel reuse at the actual mounting points is the only reliable basis for AP placement and power settings.

choices.text: Because metal racking attenuates and reflects RF unpredictably, so placement must be validated with real measurements
Because predictive tools cannot calculate coverage for more than one floor
Because a survey is required before any 802.11ax access point can be powered
Because an on-site survey removes the need to plan channel reuse

stem: Clients are spread evenly around an access point mounted in the center of an open office floor. Which antenna pattern suits that placement?
explanation: An omnidirectional antenna radiates roughly equally in all horizontal directions, forming a doughnut-shaped pattern, which covers clients surrounding the AP. A patch or Yagi concentrates energy in one direction and is used for corridors or point-to-point bridges.

choices.text: A directional patch aimed across the floor
An omnidirectional antenna radiating in all horizontal directions
A Yagi aimed at a distant building
A parabolic dish pointed down at the desks

stem: Under the cloud shared-responsibility model, which task stays with the customer in an IaaS deployment?
explanation: The provider owns the facility, hardware, and hypervisor; the customer owns the guest operating system, its patching, the identities, the data, and the security-group rules. The split moves up the stack for PaaS and SaaS but never disappears.

choices.text: Patching the guest operating system and hardening the workloads
Physical security of the data center building
Firmware updates on the hypervisor hosts
Maintenance of the underlying storage arrays

stem: Why is CSMA/CD not needed on a modern full-duplex switched Ethernet link?
explanation: Full duplex gives the interface separate transmit and receive paths, so a station can send and receive at the same time and a collision cannot occur. CSMA/CD exists only to arbitrate a shared half-duplex medium.

choices.text: Because full duplex uses separate transmit and receive paths, so collisions cannot occur
Because switches buffer every frame and retransmit any that are damaged
Because the Ethernet frame no longer carries a preamble or start frame delimiter
Because CSMA/CD was replaced by CSMA/CA on copper links

stem: A branch has only a geostationary satellite link, with the satellite about 36,000 km away. Which round-trip latency should be expected?
explanation: The signal travels about 36,000 km up and 36,000 km down at roughly 300,000 km/s, so each hop costs about 120 ms and the station-to-station path is about 240 ms one way. A round trip is therefore in the 500-600 ms range once processing is added.

choices.text: Under 5 ms
20 to 40 ms
500 to 600 ms
Over 2,000 ms

stem: A team stores nightly device backups that must be retrieved by key over an HTTPS API from any region and never modified in place. Which storage type fits?
explanation: Object storage keeps each item with metadata and a unique key in a flat namespace and is reached over HTTP, which suits immutable backups and archives. Block storage presents a raw volume that only an attached host can mount.

choices.text: Object storage addressed by key over an HTTP API
A block volume attached to a single virtual machine
A file share mounted over NFS inside one VPC
A RAM disk on the hypervisor host

stem: An engineer must carve 100, 50, 25, and 10 host subnets out of 192.168.10.0/24 with VLSM. Why allocate the 100-host subnet first?
explanation: Every subnet must sit on a boundary that matches its own mask, so allocating the largest block first guarantees it a contiguous aligned range and leaves the remainder splittable into the smaller blocks. Starting small scatters prefixes across the space and can leave no aligned range large enough for the big subnet.

Because taking the largest aligned block first prevents fragmentation from leaving no room for it
Because the first subnet allocated automatically becomes the summary route
Because smaller subnets cannot be entered in the routing table before larger ones

stem: One switch port is hardcoded to 100 Mb/s full duplex while its peer is left on auto. The link comes up at 100 Mb/s half duplex. Why?
explanation: A hardcoded port sends no fast link pulses, so the auto side has nothing to negotiate against and falls back to parallel detection, which can only infer speed from the received signal. With no duplex information available it defaults to half duplex, which produces a mismatch that shows up as late collisions on one side and FCS errors on the other.

Because the hardcoded side advertises half duplex as its highest priority
Because the cable is wired as a crossover instead of a straight-through

stem: An access point transmits at 20 dBm, the cable and connectors lose 3 dB, and the antenna has 9 dBi of gain. What is the effective isotropic radiated power?
explanation: EIRP is transmit power minus cable loss plus antenna gain: 20 - 3 + 9 = 26 dBm. The figure is what regulatory limits are written against, so it is the number that must be compared to the local cap rather than the radio's configured power.

26 dBm
32 dBm
14 dBm

stem: A host sends a TCP segment with the RST flag set on a connection that is already established. What is the effect?
explanation: RST is the abort signal. Unlike the graceful FIN exchange, it tears the connection down at once: both sides flush queued data, free the socket, and no closing handshake takes place. Applications see this as a connection reset.

choices.text: The connection is torn down immediately and any queued data is discarded
The receiver retransmits the last unacknowledged segment
The segment is held until the receive window opens
Only the sequence number is reset and the connection continues

stem: Why is a residential DSL circuit described as asymmetric?
explanation: ADSL divides the copper pair into frequency bands and allocates far more spectrum to the downstream direction than to the upstream direction, matching consumer behaviour where downloads dominate. The asymmetry is a provisioning choice, not a limitation of the line itself.

choices.text: Because downstream throughput is provisioned higher than upstream throughput
Because upstream and downstream share a single frequency band
Because the circuit can serve only one host at a time
Because the line is always on and never dials

stem: On a Cisco ASA, traffic moves from a security-level 100 interface to a security-level 50 interface and no ACL is applied. What happens by default?
explanation: The ASA permits traffic from a higher security level to a lower one without an ACL. The reverse direction is denied unless an ACL permits it or inspection state already exists from the outbound flow. That default is what makes the inside-to-outside path work out of the box.

choices.text: It is permitted, because higher-to-lower is allowed by default
It is dropped by the implicit deny

It is inspected, then dropped unless an ACL permits it

stem: A traceroute prints `* * *` for one hop and then resolves later hops normally. What does that tell you?
explanation: Routers commonly rate-limit or filter the generation of ICMP time-exceeded messages while still forwarding packets. Since later hops answer, the path is working; a bare `* * *` alone is not evidence of a forwarding failure.

choices.text: That hop did not return an ICMP time-exceeded reply, which by itself does not mean forwarding is broken
That the destination is unreachable and the trace should be abandoned
That the hop has no route back to the source, so it drops all transit traffic
That the hop is administratively shut down

stem: How does a lightweight access point in local mode handle client data traffic?
explanation: Local mode is centralized data forwarding: the AP encapsulates client frames in CAPWAP and sends them to the WLC, which bridges them to the wired network. FlexConnect is the mode that switches traffic locally at the AP instead.

choices.text: It encapsulates the client frames in CAPWAP and sends them to the WLC
It bridges them directly onto the access switch at the AP

It forwards them between clients without involving the WLC

stem: A provider assigns the prefix 2001:db8:acad:1200::/56. How many /64 subnets can the customer create from it?
explanation: The difference between /56 and /64 is 8 bits, and 2^8 is 256. Each of those /64s has 64 host bits available, which is the standard subnet size for SLAAC.

stem: In a VXLAN overlay, what does a VTEP do?
explanation: The VXLAN Tunnel Endpoint encapsulates the original Layer 2 frame inside a UDP/IP packet stamped with a VNI and sends it across the routed underlay; the remote VTEP strips the outer headers and delivers the original frame. The underlay only ever routes the outer IP header.

choices.text: It encapsulates the original Layer 2 frame in UDP/IP and forwards it across the underlay
It assigns IP addresses to the virtual machines on the segment
It terminates the storage area network for the hypervisor cluster
It load-balances traffic between the physical leaf switches

stem: What is the role of the standby controller in an N+1 wireless design?
explanation: N+1 means one backup controller covers N primaries. The standby stays synchronized and ready to accept access points if a primary fails, but while the primary is healthy it carries no client traffic. That is different from an active/active pair that shares load.

choices.text: It stays ready to take over the access points if the primary fails, carrying no client traffic while the primary is healthy

It serves only guest SSIDs while the primary serves corporate SSIDs

stem: What does a cloud scrubbing center do during a volumetric DDoS attack?
explanation: The customer advertises the attacked prefix to the scrubbing provider over BGP, traffic is drawn to the provider's cleaning infrastructure, malicious flows are dropped, and clean traffic is returned, usually through a tunnel. The origin never sees the flood.

stem: A client reports a signal level of -67 dBm and a noise floor of -92 dBm. What is the SNR?
explanation: SNR is the difference between signal and noise in dB: -67 minus -92 equals 25 dB. Because both figures are already logarithmic, they are subtracted rather than divided, and 25 dB is a healthy margin for typical data rates.

stem: What is a passive twinax DAC cable used for?
explanation: A direct-attach copper assembly is factory-terminated twinax with fixed transceivers on both ends. It carries 10, 25, 40, or 100 Gbps over a few metres between adjacent switches or servers at lower cost and power than optical modules. Being passive, it has no active electronics to equalize the signal.

stem: In DMVPN Phase 3, how does one spoke learn the public address of another spoke so it can build a direct tunnel?
explanation: The spoke asks NHRP on the hub, which acts as the next-hop server and returns the peer's NBMA address; the spoke then builds a direct mGRE tunnel to that address. Phase 3 also has the hub send a redirect so the first packets do not have to be relayed.

stem: Which statement describes how WMM (802.11e) prioritizes wireless traffic?
explanation: WMM sorts frames into four access categories (voice, video, best effort, background) and gives each its own EDCA parameters: a shorter arbitration inter-frame spacing and a smaller contention window for the higher categories, so they win the medium more often. stem: A path offers 100 Mbps of bandwidth with an 80 ms round-trip time. What is the approximate bandwidth-delay product?
explanation: 100 Mbps is 12.5 MB/s, and multiplying by 0.08 s gives about 1 MB. That is how much data must be in flight to keep the pipe full, so a TCP window smaller than roughly 1,000,000 bytes caps throughput well below the link rate no matter how much bandwidth is available.

About 8,000,000 bytes
About 125,000 bytes

stem: In a two-tier spine-leaf fabric, a host on one leaf sends a frame to a host on a different leaf. How many spine switches does that traffic cross?
explanation: Every leaf is cabled to every spine and there are no spine-to-spine links, so a leaf-to-leaf path is exactly two hops: leaf to one spine and back down to the other leaf. stem: Which term describes the coverage area of a single access point radio, within which a client can associate and pass traffic?
explanation: The basic service area is the physical footprint of one AP radio cell. The basic service set is the set of stations inside it, the BSSID names that AP radio, and an extended service set is several BSAs joined by the distribution system.

Distribution system (DS)

stem: How many usable host addresses does an IPv4 /30 subnet provide?
explanation: A /30 leaves two host bits, so the block holds four addresses. One is the network address and one is the broadcast, which leaves two usable addresses. That is why /30 is popular on point-to-point links.

stem: Which device sits in a hardened segment and is the only host administrators may log into before reaching servers in a protected internal network?
explanation: A bastion host, also called a jump host, is deliberately exposed and hardened so it can be the single controlled entry point for management access. Administrators hop through it into the protected network, so the internal servers never accept direct administrative sessions from untrusted networks.

choices.text: A bastion (jump) host
An inline intrusion prevention system
A server load balancer
A Layer 2 access switch

stem: TIA/EIA structured cabling limits a horizontal copper cable run from the telecommunications room to the work area outlet to what maximum length?
explanation: The permanent link is capped at 90 m. The 10 m of patch cords at the two ends bring the full channel to the familiar 100 m limit, which is why the two numbers are often confused.

stem: In a fiber-optic cable, what is the function of the cladding around the core?
explanation: The core has the higher refractive index and the cladding the lower one. Light arriving at that boundary at a shallow angle is totally internally reflected back into the core, which is what turns the fiber into a waveguide. Strength members and buffers protect the cable but do not guide light.

It provides a metallic shield that blocks electromagnetic interference

stem: A campus is being redesigned so that each building routes to the core instead of extending VLANs across the whole campus. What is the main benefit of pushing Layer 3 closer to the access layer?
explanation: Routing at each building bounds both the broadcast domain and the spanning-tree topology to that building. stem: A firewall is inserted into an existing subnet without readdressing any hosts or changing their default gateway. Which operating mode does this require?
explanation: In transparent mode the firewall bridges its interfaces, so it holds no address on the data path and hosts keep the same gateway. choices.text: Transparent (Layer 2) mode

stem: An access point advertises the same SSID on 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz. Clients at the far edge of the cell associate on 2.4 GHz but fail on 5 GHz. Why?

5 GHz channels overlap each other and interfere

stem: In a spine-leaf fabric, which role does a border leaf perform?
explanation: Ordinary leafs only attach servers and storage. The border leaf provides the fabric's exit point to external networks such as a WAN router or the internet edge. stem: An application runs as several identical instances in one public cloud region. Why should they be placed in different availability zones rather than all in one?
explanation: An availability zone is an isolated fault domain with its own power, cooling, and networking.
